description: Possible Roman religious complex consisting of two structures identified as 'shrines', and another thought to be a hostel. Possibly more to the south but excavation was limited. The full date range is uncertain, the excavation only investigated 4th CE layers, but 2nd CE potter was present, and it is thought the site was maintained into the Anglo-Saxon period.
bibliography: Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “West Heslerton Shrine (North Yorkshire).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
Powlesland, D. “West Heslerton Assessment” Internet Archaeology, no. 5 (1998). https://intarch.ac.uk/journal/issue5/westhes_index.html.
